utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Oh, nice — how’s the repair drive going so far? I can keep an eye out for anyone who needs help while I’m out.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: It’s going steady so far, Ira, but I’d feel better with a clear list. If you spot anyone who needs help, just send them my way or jot down their name for me.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: You got it — I’ll jot down any names I hear and send them your way. I’m headed out now, so I’ll keep an eye out.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Leo, I’m a bit slammed, but I caught the repair drive note—what’s the main thing you need from me?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Mostly need you to spread the word and send anyone who’s handy. If you can swing by for a bit, that’d help too.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Got it—I'll mention it to a few handy folks on the block and try to swing by if I can carve out time.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Before I sign on, can you confirm exactly what’s being repaired and who’s collecting the money?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I’d want that nailed down too—let’s ask for a written list of repairs and the treasurer’s name before anyone hands over money.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Good, I’m not comfortable contributing until we’ve got that in writing and can confirm the treasurer is actually handling it.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh, right—the repair drive. I was meaning to stop by, but I forgot what I was bringing. Did you need help with anything specific?

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Yes, could you bring any spare screws, duct tape, or a flashlight? I’m keeping track of what we still need.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Sure thing, Cleo—I know I’ve got duct tape and probably a flashlight somewhere, and I’ll check my junk drawer for spare screws before I come by.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Hi Noah, before we get started, can you remind me which repairs are the top priority for the drive?

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh, right — I think the top priorities were the leaky faucet, the broken porch step, and that flickering hallway light. I might be missing one, though.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Thanks, Noah — I’ll note those three, but let’s double-check the list before we act so we don’t miss that possible fourth repair.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Hey Jules, sorry I’m late—what’s the latest on the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: No worries, Dane — we’ve got the tool table almost sorted, and I’m checking who can cover small appliance repairs versus bike fixes. If you know anyone handy, send them my way!

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Got it—I can ask Marco about small appliances, and I’m happy to jump in wherever you’re short.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: I’m happy to help with the repair drive—what do you need from me?

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Thanks, Sam — could you bring your drill and maybe a hammer? That would help a lot with the repair drive.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Absolutely, Gus — I’ll bring my drill and a hammer for the repair drive.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Hi Faye, I’m just getting my bearings for the repair drive—do we know where the drop-off table and tool station are being set up?

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Hi Opal — I don’t have the exact setup yet, but I can check with the school office and see where they’re putting the drop-off table and tool station. I’ll let you know as soon as I find out.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Thanks, Faye — I’d appreciate that. I’m keeping track of the setup spots, so just let me know when you hear back.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Hi Quinn, have you heard how the repair drive is shaping up? I’m trying to gather the latest so I can spread the word properly.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: It’s coming together nicely — folks are pitching in and it’s starting to look like a real neighborhood effort. I’ll keep passing the word along so everyone knows how to join in.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh, that’s wonderful to hear, Quinn — I’ll tell folks it’s gaining steam and there’s room for everyone to lend a hand.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Rey, what exactly still needs fixing, and who’s already signed up to help?

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I’ve only heard a few bits so far, Mina — I need to check the full list before I can say for sure who’s signed up. I’ll ask around and tell you what I learn.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Alright, Rey—please get me the full list and the names by this afternoon if you can, so we know where the gaps are.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: I’ll spread the word about the repair drive and remind folks to bring anything they can. We can make sure everyone knows the time and place.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: That sounds great, Vik—thank you. I’ll check with a couple people nearby too, just in case they’ve heard of anyone who needs help getting items over.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Thanks, Nell—I’ll keep spreading the word and remind everyone to bring whatever they can. I’ll make sure the time and place are clear too.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Uli, I’m glad we’re getting the repair drive moving—are you able to help me pin down what items neighbors most need fixed?

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: I can help with that, Rosa. I’ll ask around quietly and make a short list of the things people mention most.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Thanks, Uli—that would be a big help. Bring me the list when you have it, and I’ll organize the repairs from there.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Hi Eli, have you heard when the repair drive is kicking off? I’ve been trying to keep folks in the loop.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Hi Tess, I haven’t heard a firm time yet. If you can get me the schedule, I’ll help spread the word after my morning walk.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Thanks, Eli — I’ll check on the schedule and let you know as soon as I hear, so you can pass it along after your walk.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Hey, sorry I’m late — how’s the repair drive going?

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: No worries, Dane — it’s just getting started, and folks are already talking about who’s bringing what tools. I can help spread the plan once we’ve got the details nailed down.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Thanks, Vik — that’d help a lot. What tools are we short on so I can ask around?

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Hi Uli, I haven’t heard much about the repair drive yet. What’s needed most right now?

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: Mostly volunteers and a few basic supplies. I’m still sorting through things on my end, but I can share the list if that helps.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Yes, please share the list when you can. I’m better at helping once I know the specific gaps.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Opal, I’m a bit slammed, but I heard there’s a repair drive happening—what’s the quick version?

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Quick version: folks are collecting broken household items for repair, and I’m keeping track of who’s bringing what and where it’s being dropped off.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Got it—so if I’ve got a busted toaster and maybe a lamp, do I just tell you and drop them somewhere?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Hey Hana, I’m glad we’re doing the repair drive. I can help spread the word and line up a few neighbors too.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Thanks, Jules, that would help a lot. Before we start spreading the word, can we confirm the date, location, and what kinds of repairs we’re accepting?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Absolutely—let’s lock those in first. What date and location are you leaning toward, and are we keeping it to small appliances, bikes, clothing, and simple electronics?

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh, right, the repair drive—sorry, I’m a little scattered today. What still needs doing for it?

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: No worries — we still need a few hands to sort the donated tools, set up the tables, and greet folks when they arrive. If you want, I can put you on one of those.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Could you put me on sorting the donated tools? I might be a bit slow to start, but I can handle that.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Hey Gus, I’m just catching up while I’m out—what’s the latest on the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Hey Ira, we’re gathering tools and small parts this week, then setting up the tables Saturday morning. I can bring my socket set and cordless drill if you’ve got a list going.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: That’s great, Gus—I'll note you down for the socket set and cordless drill, and I’ll ask around for any small parts folks can spare.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Hey Leo, I’m glad you brought up the repair drive—what do you need help with first?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: First thing is sorting the broken items by type. If you can take electronics, I’ll handle tools and small appliances.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Absolutely, I’ll take the electronics and start grouping them by type and condition. If I spot anything dangerous or leaking batteries, I’ll set it aside and let you know.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Before we get too excited, do we know where the repair drive would actually be held and who’s bringing the tools?

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Good questions. Do we have permission to use the community room, and can we make a list of who owns basic tools before we pick a date?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Yes, let’s not pick a date until the room is confirmed; I can ask the building office about availability, but someone should start the tool list too.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Hey Cleo, I’m helping spread the word about the repair drive—want me to put you on the invite list or pass along the details?

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Yes, please put me on the invite list, Quinn. I’d also like the details so I can see what supplies we might need to gather.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Absolutely, Cleo—I’ll add you to the invite list and send over the time, location, and supply notes as soon as I have them.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Hi Oren, I’m trying to line up the repair drive around school pickup times—do you know what time you’re thinking of starting?

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh, right—the repair drive. I was thinking of starting around 3:30, after the school pickup rush, if that works.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: 3:30 works well for me—thanks for avoiding the pickup crunch. I can help spread the word to the other parents.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Nell, I’m glad we could connect about the repair drive—I'd love to hear what you think our neighbors most need fixed first.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Hi Rosa, I’m still catching up from what folks have been telling me, but I’ve heard a few mentions of broken porch lights and loose handrails. I’d love to know if that matches what you’ve been hearing too.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Yes, that lines up with what I’ve heard too—porch lights for safety after dark, and handrails especially for our older neighbors. I’ll start a simple priority list with those at the top and keep gathering names.
